reference.title: How onCall Handle Alarms
reference.shortdesc: The topic explains how the OnCallRecipient receives an alarm. When an alarm is raised, the On Call user receives a notification based on the priority and configured time.

section.p: When an OnCallRecipient receives an alarm, it is routed to the current OnCallList.

The OnCallList sends the alarm to the OnCallContact with the highest priority. (Here, a low number means a high priority. An OnCallContact with priority 1 will receive the alarm before an OnCallContact with priority 2.) If multiple OnCall contacts share the same priority number, they are contacted simultaneously.

When the alarm is sent, a timer starts. The user or users notified have a set amount of time to acknowledge the alarm (Refer to for more details.) If this time elapses and the alarm is not acknowledged, the next users down the line, in priority order, are notified, and the timer starts again. This process continues until either the alarm is acknowledged or there are no more users to notify.

To configure how much time users have to acknowledge alarms, change the Escalation Delay property in the OnCallRecipient. It defaults to 30 minutes, meaning an on-call user has 30 minutes to acknowledge An alarm is triggered before contacting the next on-call user.
